senses.gloss: סֵירס (cmp. הָרַס, רָסַס) to destroy, uproot; to mutilate, esp. to make impotent.
units: <cite ref="Tosefta Bava Batra 4:7">Tosef. B. Bath. IV, 7</cite> <he>חלות דבש אינו רשאי לסָרֵס וכ׳</he> ed. Zuck. (oth. ed. <he>לירש</he>) if the honey-combs of a bee-hive are sold, the purchaser must not uproot (tear out) all of them at the same time, but must leave the outermost cakes &c.
<cite ref="Sotah 36a:9">Sot. 36ᵃ</cite> <he>סֵירְסַתָּן מלמטה</he> it (the wasp <cite ref="R00794"><he>צִרְעָה</he></cite>) mutilated them at their lower extremities.
<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:1">Cant. R. to I, 1</cite> <he>סֵירְסוֹ</he> made him impotent.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 25a:3">Kidd. 25ᵃ</cite> <he>עבד שסִרְסוֹ וכ׳</he> a slave whom his master mutilated by injury to his testicles.
<cite ref="Shabbat 110b:6">Sabb. 110ᵇ</cite> <he>הרוצה שיְסָרֵס וכ׳</he> if one desires to emasculate a cock, let him take off his comb, and he will thereby be emasculated (without an operation).
<cite ref="Shabbat 111a:1">Ib. 111ᵃ</cite> <he>במְסָרֵס אחר מסרס</he> if one adds to the mutilation caused by another person; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Batra 5:3">B. Bath. V, 3</cite> <he>נוטל ג׳ נחלין ומסרס</he> the buyer takes three broods, after which the owner may make the bees impotent of propagation; <cite ref="Bava Batra 80a:4">ib. 80ᵃ</cite> <he>במה מְסָרְסָן וכ׳</he> by what means does one make them impotent?… By feeding them with mustard.
Ib. לא חרדל מסרסן וכ׳ mustard does not make them impotent &c.—Trnsf. to disarrange, upset; to transpose.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 80a:1-5">Ib.</cite> (another interpret. of <he>ומסרס</he>, Mish. l. c.) <he>נוטל … בסירוס</he>, v. <cite ref="O00841"><he>סֵירוּס</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Bava Batra 119b:6">Ib. 119ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Numbers 27:2">Num. XXVII, 2</cite>) <he>סָרֵס המקרא ודרשהו</he> invert the order in which the persons are mentioned in that verse, and interpret it.

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 27:1">Lev. R. s. 27</cite>, beg. (ref. to <cite ref="Psalms 36:7">Ps. XXXVI, 7</cite>) <he>סרס המקרא וכ׳</he> transpose the verse, and explain it: ‘thy kindness is as far above thy judgments, as the mountains are above the great deep’.

Ex. R. s. 5 (ref. to מי, Ex. V, 2) סרס אותו מי ים וכ׳ transpose mi and read yam, the sea made thee know the Lord; a. fr.—[Lev. R. s. 12 מסרסתו, read: מְסַטַּרְתּוֹ, v. סָטַר.]—Part. pass. מְסוֹרָס upside down, transposed &c.
<cite ref="Mishnah Niddah 3:5">Nidd. III, 5</cite> <he>יצא … מס׳</he> if the embryo came out with its feet foremost.

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 11:4">Num. R. s. 11</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Exodus 20:24">Ex. XX, 24</cite>) <he>זה מקרא מס׳ וכ׳</he> this verse must be interpreted by transposition, wherever I shall come and bless thee, there I shall allow my Name (the Tetragrammaton) to be pronounced. Mekh. B’shall., Vayass‘a, s. 4.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 70">Gen. R. s. 70</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 28:22">Gen. XXVIII, 22</cite>) <he>מְסוֹרֶסֶת היא הפרשה</he> the accounts of the section are not in chronological order, opp. <he>על הסדר וכ׳</he>; a. e.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 86">Gen. R. s. 86</cite>; a. e.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 93b:12">Snh. 93ᵇ</cite> <he>נִסְתָּרְסָה ע״ז וכ׳</he> idolatry was uprooted in their days (in the days of Hanania, Mishael &c.). Mekh. Mishp. s. 20 [read:] <he>שלא תִסְתָּרֵס שבת בראשית ממקומה</he> to intimate that the weekly Sabbath is not to be removed from its place, i.e. that it must be observed also in the Sabbatical year; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 354">Yalk. Ex. 354</cite>. Mekh. l. c. <he>שלא יִסְתָּרְסוּ שלש וכ׳</he> that the three festivals must not be removed from their place; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 356:3">Yalk. Ex. 356</cite> <he>שלא יסתרו וכ׳</he> (corr. acc.).
